recipes.name: Italian Meatball Sandwich Casserole
ingredients_raw: 1 (1 pound) loaf Italian bread, cut into 1-inch cubes

steps.text: Gather the ingredients. Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (205 degrees C).

Mix onions, bread crumbs, Parmesan cheese, and ground beef together in a bowl. Roll mixture into even-sized meatballs, about 1 inch in diameter; place in a baking pan. Bake in the preheated oven until beef is no longer pink, 15 to 20 minutes. Reduce the oven temperature to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

Arrange bread cubes in a single layer in an ungreased 9x13-inch baking dish. Mix cream cheese, mayonnaise, Italian seasoning, and black pepper together until smooth. Spread this mixture over each bread cube. Sprinkle with 1/2 cup of the grated mozzarella cheese.

Mix spaghetti sauce, water (if using), and garlic together in a large bowl. Gently stir in meatballs; pour over bread and cheese mixture in the baking pan. Sprinkle remaining mozzarella cheese evenly over the top.
Bake at 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) for 30 minutes, or until heated through.

raw_recipe.headline: Italian Meatball Sandwich Casserole
raw_recipe.description: This Italian meatball sandwich casserole layers Italian bread with homemade meatballs, tomato sauce, and plenty of melted mozzarella cheese.

review.reviewBody:
I know some hate when others post reviews that tell all about what they did differently, but I figure...hey, many people have made this & found it to be great....so why not tell what I did...maybe it will inspire you!!!
1.) I made my meatballs out of ground chicken! They only need 15 mins. at 400..just be sure to lightly spray your sheet with cooking spray! I also combined the minced garlic in with my chickenballs....
2.) As another reviewer suggested...I omitted the mayo & replaced it with ricotta...did I mention that the ricotta/cream cheese mixture was good enough to spread on my body?!?!
3.)Probably the biggest change I made was how I used the bread....I bought the roundish italian loaf, did my best Subway sandwhich artist impression, and removed the top portion. I then removed most (but not all) the fluffy bread guts to make a bowl (and tossed the guts). I smeared the cream/ricotta cheese mixture on the bottom & sides of the bowl, and added some to the underside of the breadbowl lid. (This way b/c I thought spreading each breadcube with the mixture sounded too time consuming...and half the breadcubes prolly would of ended up popped in my mouth!!!) I then layered the cheese & chicken balls, baked 25 minutes WITHOUT the breadbowl lid, and about 5-10 with the breadbowl lid in place...to serve, just slice....my "boys" (my fiance & his best friend) raved over this for at least an hour....and they are food snobs!!!!

Really good with my changes: 1) I subbed ricotta for mayo, 2) added dried minced onions and a little more Italian seasoning to the cream cheese/ricotta mixture, 3) toasted and cut the bread in half then spread the cheese mixture on it, 4) omitted the water and added a little Italian seasoning to the sauce, 5) heated some frozen meatballs and sliced them before laying them on top of the bread and cheeses, 6) sprinkled more mozzarella on the meatballs and covered them with the sauce. Family liked it a lot!

This was delicious. I read a ton of reviews and changed the following 3 things: I omitted the water completely, swapped the mayo out for ricotta cheese and toasted the bread in the baking dish before topping it with the cheese/sauce. The bread was still soft but not overly mushy. Everyone cleaned their plates and wanted more (good thing this makes plenty!) Will make this again, definitely (I want to try Garlic Texas Toast next time) :)

I'm rating this based upon how I made it after reading many reviews and working with what I had in the fridge, and it was AWESOME! My hubby stopped mid-meal, and said "yeah, that recipe's a keeper." I scaled the recipe down for two because I had a bread bowl that needed to be used, so I hollowed it out as another cook suggested, and smeared the cream cheese-cottage cheese mixture together (I wasn't going for the mayo, and I didn't have ricotta) on the inside of the bowl and the underside of the "lid". I used pre-made meatballs, thawed and sliced, mixed into about 6 oz. of a four cheese tomato canned sauce, filled the bowl with that, and topped it with an Italian cheese blend. I baked it without the lid for about 20 minutes, then added the lid for another ten. I sliced it, and it kind of fell apart, but the taste more than made up for the less than restaurant quality presentation. It really was like a baked Italian meatball sub, and reminded the hubby of when we lived in MA, where grinders are everywhere. I'll be making this at least once every couple of weeks during the cold months. Thanks for submitting the recipe, and thanks to all the reviewers.

A great recipe, but I would exchange cream cheese and mayo for Ricotta cheese; the combination of Ricotta and Mozzarella is fabulous! Instead of coating the bread cubes, would it be faster to just spread the cheese mixture thickly over the bread halves, sides and all, pour the sauce mixture over them and add the remaining cheese mixture to the top? You can cut each serving after it’s cooked. This is the best recipe I have found, though, for an Italian Meatball Sandwich! And, next to homemade Lasagna, that is my very favorite Italian food! Even over Pizza, which I would almost kill for! Thank you for sharing it! It is going into my cookbook as a favorite!!!

Wow what an amazing idea to create a casserole out of an already wonderful meal! My family loves casseroles, my son especially anything meaty, saucey, cheesy. It is highly customizable as well. I made my own meatballs using crushed croutons, a recipe I found on the website. I didn’t have mayo so I used plain Greek yogurt in its place. I spread the mixture over the 2”x1” bread cubes to make a layer. And I didn’t use water/garlic in the sauce. Mmmmmmm

Just made this tonight and my husband and i loved it! I followed other reviewers and subd ricotta cheese for the mayo, omited the water, and used garlic bread baked crunchy first. Also added some chopped bells peppers. Yum! Will make again!

This recipe has been in my recipe box for over 8 years (a third of my life) and I FINALLY made it tonight! I wish I'd tried it earlier because it is very, very tasty and my husband and I went crazy over it. I used one of those long French baguettes from the grocery store bakery instead of Italian bread because we like it more and it is sturdier than Italian bread. I also used frozen vegetarian meatballs because my husband wants to try eating vegetarian for a while, I left out the water (that would have made it too soggy for us, I can tell). For the spaghetti sauce, I used my own pizza sauce recipe. If anyone wants it, it's 3 cups plain tomato sauce (I use Hunt's because I like the flavor and it's already kind of salty, you may need to add salt if you use a different brand), 1 1/2 t oregano, 1 1/2 t basil, 3/4 t rosemary, 3/4 t garlic powder, 3/4 t onion powder, and 3/4 t pepper stirred together. Very simple. Prepared as I did, the bread is a little toasty on the bottom and the sauce moistens the bread but doesn't make it soggy. Soggy bread gives me the willies (I don't like stuffing or bread pudding), but this was very good. The flavor of the cream cheese and mayo is really good too, try it with the mayo before changing it because you can't specifically taste the mayo but the mixture tastes great. It's creamy, tangy, and smooth and really adds something. I'm sure ricotta would be good too, but the resulting flavor of the casserole would be changed a lot.
Used ricotta instead of cream cheese, added beaten egg instead of mayonaise, 1/4c. of water to beaten egg.

Okay so I tweet this recipe by first frying some green peppers and onions in a pot then adding some garlic and then throwing in the meatballs which were frozen and adding a half large jar of spaghetti sauce. I pre-baked my Frozen garlic bread eight pieces and cook them a little bit on the Crouton side. So they pretty much came out soft but firmly baked crouton layer on the outside. After wedding chapel for about 5:00 I then cut them into cubes the size of large croutons . After about 20 minutes of slow simmering under low medium Heat I spooned out meatballs into a half pan adding sauce where needed. Filling the half pan halfway with the meatballs sauce I then poured on half a large container of jalapeno queso softened in the microwave to where you can pour it and then layered shredded mozzarella and Parmesan. I've been spooned a little excess sauce on top of the cheese just for color and placed in an oven 350° for 15 minutes or until the top layer of cheese starts to Brown. I then take the pan out of the oven and layer the pieces of garlic bread on top of the cheese and gently press the bread into the softened warm cheese. Loosely cover the pan with aluminum foil tucking it in and places but leaving a space for it to breathe so it does not soften your bread too much. Bake for an additional 15 minutes and then remove from oven. I made it like this and it came out really well the bread did not get soggy

I sliced the bread and spread the cream cheese mixture between two slices and then diced them and added them to the pan. Seemed easier than trying to spread across the top. I used pre cooked Italian meatballs as a timesaver. My family loved it. Will put in our winter rotation.
I made this tonight. My wife is glutten sensitive so I used GF pasta instead of the bread. My family really liked it.
Yummy

We didn't have enough bread to cover the bottom of the pan so we used king's Hawaiian bowl bread. It made it a little sweeter and I totally recommend the Hawaiian bread. We used the bowl bread bc that was the only thing we had but you can use the rolls or whatever! Definitely would make this again!
My family tried this for the first time tonight. And now it's going to go into the rotation.
So I did two small ones at first and the original recipe was soggy,But using Texas toast and Ricotta cheese worked great… I also used way less sauce

I hate it when people modify a recipe but based on everyone's reviews on this and after reading them, I felt I had too. The reason I even tried it after the reviews was if I could modify it, the family loves meatball sandwiches; however, my end result is: I would not make this again. The flavor wasn't bad but, the bread still turned out soggy. These were my modifications based on problems others experienced. 1. Preheat oven to 400 degrees F (205 degrees C). 2. Meatballs. Mix together onions, bread crumbs, Parmesan cheese and ground beef. Roll into 1 inch diameter balls, and place in a baking pan. Bake for 15 to 20 minutes, or until beef is no longer pink. (I made my own meatballs (recipe below) Reduce the oven temperature to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). 3. Bread Cubes. Arrange the bread cubes in a single layer in an ungreased 9x13 inch baking dish. I ripped one large baguette up and toasted it in the oven first at 385 for 10 minutes, just to crisp up the bread, turning the bread cubes so they don’t burn. 4. Cheese Mixture. Mix together the cream cheese, mayonnaise (I didn’t use cream cheese and mayo) I used 8 oz Ricotta), Italian seasoning, Parm cheese and black pepper until smooth. Spread this mixture over each bread cube (I put dollops of Ricotta mixture all over as the cheese will melt. 5. Mozzerella. Sprinkle with 1/2 cup of the grated mozzarella cheese. 6. Sauce and Meatballs. In a large bowl, mix together spaghetti sauce, water (didn’t use), and garlic. Gently stir in meatballs. Pour over the bread and cheese mixture in the baking pan. Sprinkle the remaining mozzarella cheese evenly over the top. 7. Bake at 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) for 30 minutes, or until heated through. I made my own meatballs.
Very good! The only thing I changed was the warmest cheese bc my mom doesn't like it so used more shredded matzerella in it. Everything else I followed. Thanks for sharing!!

I followed the recipe pretty closely, except that I only had regular sliced bread. I toasted it in the oven at the same time I cooked the meatballs. The bread was still soggy in places, but crunchy in others. Will keep the bread intact next time and just spread the mayo mixture on it. Hubby liked it, so I'll try again.
This was HIGHLY received by my family but with changes due to preference AND convenience. Very good with modifications!!
